_note: Product-by-product fire evidence for the public table on /advice/wallcovering-fire-ratings-uk/. One row per product or product family, never per brand. classificationRaw is the fire line as printed; notation is the class copied from it (null when two documents disagree); classification repeats only what the notation prints. Rows were selected from the research records in docs/research/fire-ratings/manufacturers/ (checked 15 Oct 2026); see that folder for every product examined.

products.product: Fabric-backed vinyl, Type II, 460 gsm (woven and non-woven backings)
products.scope: The two 460 gsm Type II product types listed in the declaration. No product codes or colourways are listed; Muraspec says the product code is on the packaging.
products.construction: Vinyl on woven or non-woven fabric backing, Type II
products.classificationRaw: B-s2, d0 on fibre cement board attached with Murabond heavy adhesive

testedBuildup.other: No primer, lining, air gap or fixing is stated.

limitations: The class is declared only for the fibre-cement and Murabond Heavy build-up.
The certificates listed for these rows carry printed expiry dates of 28 October and 25 November 2027.
conflicts: An earlier Muraspec declaration (CPR0002, 2024) declares B-s1,d0 for Type II non-woven fabric-backed vinyl; this 2025 declaration gives B-s2,d0.
unresolved: The classification report behind the declaration is not published.
Product pages cite 'CPR0003' without a version, and the number was also used for a different 2024 declaration.

products.product: Fabric-backed vinyl, woven Type I, 360 gsm
products.scope: One product type at 360 gsm. The product code is on the packaging; no colourways are listed.
products.construction: Vinyl on woven fabric backing, Type I
products.classificationRaw: Class B, s1, d0 (on fibre cement board using Murabond heavy adhesive)

evidence.testBody: BTTG (printed with spelling errors and two addresses)

testedBuildup.other: No primer, lining, air gap or fixing is stated.

limitations: The class is declared only for the fibre-cement and Murabond Heavy build-up.
Only 360 gsm is named.
conflicts: Another Muraspec declaration (CPR0001, 2024) declares B-s2,d0 for woven fabric-backed vinyl of 360 to 460 gsm, which overlaps this product; the two declarations give different smoke subclasses.
A product page that cites CPR0004 shows a 460 gsm product, while the declaration names only 360 gsm.
unresolved: Which of the two woven declarations applies to a given roll is not explained.
The laboratory report named in the declaration is not published.

products.scope: Two digitally printed base types, each with its own laboratory report number. The declaration says nothing about print coverage, inks or bespoke artwork.
products.construction: Digitally printed vinyl on non-woven fabric backing
products.classificationRaw: Class B, s2, d0 (on fibre cement board using Murabond heavy adhesive)

testedBuildup.other: No primer, lining, air gap or fixing is stated.

limitations: The class is declared only for the fibre-cement and Murabond Heavy build-up.
Only the two named base weights are covered.
conflicts: The declaration number CPR0003 was reused in 2025 for a different, wider declaration with another notified body.
unresolved: Whether newer digital bases (for example 410 gsm or foil bases) fall within this declaration is not stated.
How print coverage, ink or bespoke artwork affects the classification is not stated.

products.product: Buflon Mousse Anafi acoustic foam vinyl (BM-61527103)

limitations: A web page statement only, not a declaration of performance or classification report.

The panel and window-film ratings on the same sheet do not apply to the wallcovering.
unresolved: What "suitable substrate" means.
Which test report and laboratory support the class for the printed build-up.

products.product: Vinyl wallcovering, 350 g/m², plain white, not embossed
products.reference: Classification report 2023-Efectis-R000709 (August 2023); declaration of performance DOP-CPR-01006
products.scope: One plain white, non-embossed 350 g/m² vinyl as tested. Vescom files the same report under four printed (+print) design names, which the report does not describe.
products.construction: Vinyl on woven cotton backing, 0.45 mm

testedBuildup.other: Vertical joints

products.fieldOfApplication: The tested thickness, mass, colour (white, not embossed), substrate, adhesive and joints only; no wider substrate class is stated.
limitations: The field of application is a single colour, texture and adhesive.
conflicts: Filed under printed design names that the report does not cover.
Other Vescom vinyl evidence uses Vescom 2000 on 11 mm calcium silicate; this report uses Vescom 3000 on 12 mm board.
unresolved: Whether printed, coloured or embossed 350 g/m² designs fall under this report.

products.product: Cotton-backed vinyl wallcovering, FR treated, 360 to 850 g/m² (family declaration)
products.scope: A mass range, not one design. The certificate annex lists Vescom vinyl wallcoverings and digitally printed vinyl.
products.construction: Vinyl on cotton backing

testedBuildup.other: Vertical joints

products.fieldOfApplication: Calcium silicate board and other A1 or A2-s1,d0 substrates of over 652.5 kg/m³, excluding plasterboard, with vertical joints (certificate p. 2).
limitations: Plasterboard is expressly excluded from the certificate’s field of application.
A family declaration: individual designs can have their own, different results.
conflicts: The 2024 declaration gives 360–850 g/m², while the 2017 declaration and the certificate give 350–800 g/m².
A 2012 Vescom classification report on a 460 g/m² vinyl was tested on paper-faced plasterboard, which this certificate excludes.
unresolved: Whether a certificate replaced 0493-CPR-W014 after its stated validity ended.

products.reference: Product page and specsheet; linked classification report DO-18-0159
products.scope: 75 colourways with the PRO suffix, which carry the Protect film.
products.construction: Plain vinyl on woven cotton backing with Vescom Protect film

testedBuildup.substrate: Calcium silicate board, 11 mm, 870 kg/m³ (in the linked report)
testedBuildup.adhesive: Vescom 2000 at 170 g/m² (in the linked report)
testedBuildup.other: The linked report tests a different vinyl (Vescom Rainy) with no Protect layer described.

products.fieldOfApplication: In the linked report: no variation in composition; any colour and pattern; calcium silicate board and A1 or A2-s1,d0 substrates above 652.5 kg/m³, excluding plasterboard.
limitations: The specsheet and page give no standard edition, laboratory, report number, substrate or adhesive.
conflicts: The report linked from the product page never names Colour Choice or Protect and describes a vinyl without the Protect laminate.
Vescom's Protect pages describe Protect products generally as B s1 d0, while this product is listed as B s2 d0.
unresolved: Which report supports Colour Choice+Protect specifically.
Whether the linked report, printed as valid for five years from August 2018, has been renewed.

products.scope: Porak+print as tested, in any colour with or without print.
products.construction: Recycled polyester weave coated on both sides with acrylate, FR treated, 0.35 mm

testedBuildup.substrate: Non-combustible board, class A1 or A2, 870 kg/m³
testedBuildup.other: Vertical joints

products.fieldOfApplication: The tested thickness and mass, any colour with or without print, and the substrate, adhesive and joints as tested.

unresolved: Whether the printed layer on a given order matches the tested description.

products.product: Woven textile on paper backing, silk, wool and synthetic fibres (family declaration DOP-CPR-13004; tested quality 69-2341)
products.scope: Only the tested quality, colour and weave. The report was issued to the textile producer, Tapetex BV, and is in Vescom’s document library; Vescom’s declaration for this fibre family cites it.
products.construction: Woven silk, wool, polyester and nylon on a reinforced paper backing, 0.4 mm

testedBuildup.substrate: Calcium silicate board, 12 mm, 870 kg/m³, class A1
testedBuildup.adhesive: A starch and resin dispersion wallcovering adhesive at 200 g/m² wet
testedBuildup.other: No fire retardant used; vertical joints

products.fieldOfApplication: Substrates of at least 652.5 kg/m³, at least 9 mm thick and A2-s1,d0 or better, excluding paper-faced gypsum plasterboard; no air gap; vertical joints permitted; a starch and resin dispersion adhesive.
limitations: Paper-faced plasterboard is expressly excluded.
The tested adhesive is not one of the Vescom-branded adhesives.
Differences in composition, thickness, density or colour may invalidate the result for a variant.
conflicts: Three other reports on related textile qualities in the same library allow no joints at all.
unresolved: How the relationship between the textile producer and Vescom affects which declaration applies to an order.

testedBuildup.other: The classification report named in the declaration was not available to read.

products.product: Moire Sauvage (Arte Contract), contract vinyl type 07A
products.scope: The 14 Moire Sauvage references listed in the declaration. Not other Arte Contract designs, although the certificate groups them in one family.
products.construction: Vinyl on non-woven backing, Type II
products.weight: About 460 g/m² (as printed on the specification sheet)

testedBuildup.substrate: Fibre-cement board, vertical joints (density and thickness not stated)
testedBuildup.adhesive: Not stated in the declaration or certificate
testedBuildup.other: No primer, lining, air gap or fixing described.

products.fieldOfApplication: The certificate covers decorative Type II and Type III FR-treated vinyl on woven or non-woven backing, 451 to 790 g/m², glued on fibre-cement with vertical joints. No other substrate or adhesive is expressly permitted.
limitations: Nothing read extends the class to plasterboard, plaster, painted walls, lining paper or timber.
Arte's hanging instructions recommend Arte Clearpro or a dispersion adhesive; the adhesive behind the classification is not stated.
conflicts: The declaration states System 3, while the certificate it cites is issued under System 1.
The "US Class A" file linked from the product page is a 2013 test of a different product, not Moire Sauvage.
unresolved: Which adhesive and board were used in the underlying tests, which are not published.
Whether the class holds on plasterboard or painted plaster.

products.scope: The 40 Dots references listed in the declaration. The group classification report also lists other Arte collection names.
products.construction: Wallpaper on non-woven backing with relief ink dots
products.classificationStandardCited: EN 13501-1 (edition not printed in the declaration)

testedBuildup.substrate: End-use substrates of 1,350 kg/m³ or more, class A2-s1,d0 or A1
testedBuildup.other: The group report covers 130 to 592 g/m².

products.fieldOfApplication: Starch glue at 200 g/m² on substrates of at least 1,350 kg/m³ classed A2-s1,d0 or A1 (classification report). No other variation is stated.
limitations: A substrate of at least 1,350 kg/m³ is far denser than standard plasterboard; the report does not mention plasterboard, plaster or painted walls.
Arte's specification sheet recommends Clearpro or a dispersion adhesive rather than the starch glue in the report.
conflicts: The declaration is dated April 2022, but the current version of the classification report rests on tests dated July 2022.
unresolved: Whether the 2022 declaration has been checked against the current report.
Which colourways were tested.

products.scope: The Project range paper-backed vinyl as tested.
products.construction: PVC coating 290 g/m² on paper backing 90 g/m², 0.55 mm

testedBuildup.substrate: Fibre-cement board, 8 mm, 1,800 kg/m³, primed with a PVA and starch sealer at 85 g/m²
